finding_statement: The benchmark has 26.5% churn labels. Class weighting is available in documented model searches; synthetic resampling is outside the chosen protocol.
Preprocessing covers data typing, missing-value treatment, encoding, scaling, and stratified split.

Five model families share the split, preprocessing and ROC-AUC tuning objective, with unequal search budgets. Reported CV classification metrics use probability >= 0.5; post-tuning CV is internal sensitivity.
Observed holdout AUCs range from 0.836 to 0.848. Ten unadjusted pairwise comparisons are exploratory. Operational equivalence and the cause of remaining errors were not established.

XGBoost is the fixed illustrative tree explanation model in the revised workflow. This choice follows inspection of the results and does not establish a deployment winner. Brier is overall probability prediction loss.

The descriptive XGBoost sweep illustrates a contact trade-off: reducing the cutoff from 0.50 to 0.35 raises identified churners from 198 to 276 and flagged non-churners from 96 to 206. Minima are selected and described on the same sample and grid under assumed penalties.

Grouped SHAP identifies influential inputs to the fitted XGBoost model, led by Contract, tenure, InternetService, OnlineSecurity and MonthlyCharges. Permutation importance provides a complementary view of this model; neither method establishes causal drivers.

Dependence plots describe how individual inputs contribute to this fitted model across observed records. They do not estimate the effect of intervening on a field or validate communication constructs.
Local SHAP waterfall plots explain selected true-positive, false-positive, true-negative, false-negative and borderline benchmark records.

The authored communication mappings distinguish observed fields, possible interpretations, competing explanations and candidate evaluations. Platform validity and intervention effects remain untested.
The report, notebook, demo and deck are linked through exports and traceability records. The verifier checks numerical CSV agreement; narrative validity requires separate review.
Inference latency is measured on one machine and batch configuration. It does not establish production cost or a hardware-independent ordering of models.
